title: Refuse migration if validating loader skipped any on-disk records
context: The migration was silently deleting records that failed validation (corrupt/invalid/future-schema), because the load-then-wipe sequence didn't detect that the loader had skipped records. A kind with only invalid records would skip merge entirely but still get wiped. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_947c578b2c (Forward-migrate raw JSON to the current schema BEFORE Zod validation; never silently drop unmigratable records); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex).
decision: Added rawRecordCount() to count all on-disk records independent of validation. movePublicMemoryToPrivate now refuses the entire migration if rawRecordCount ≠ loadedRecordCount, proving every on-disk record loaded before allowing any deletion. Users must fix or remove problematic records, then retry.
consequences: Migration fails explicitly with actionable error when any record is corrupt/invalid/unparseable
Prevents silent permanent deletion of records that never reached the overlay
Users directed to diagnose and fix problems before retrying, not discovering loss post-operation
Migration check costs O(n) file I/O per kind (counts all files/array entries) but prevents data loss
alternatives_rejected: Silently delete invalid records (violates never-silently-drop; users lose data without knowing)
Skip merge but not delete for invalid-only kinds (leaves partial/inconsistent state)
Warn but proceed (warning may be missed; silent loss still possible)
Attempt automatic recovery/fixup (too much magic; may corrupt further)
